days.title: Meet the pieces & their moves
days.description: Learn how each of the six chess pieces (Pawn, Knight, Bishop, Rook, Queen, King) moves on the board. No board needed, just visualize.
days.tip: The Knight's 'L' shape move is often the trickiest to remember first.

days.title: Set up the board & basic captures
days.description: Set up a physical or digital chess board correctly. Practice moving pieces and capturing opponent's pieces according to their rules.
days.tip: Queens and Kings always start on their own color square.

days.title: Special moves: Castling & En Passant
days.description: Understand and practice the special moves: Castling (King and Rook) and En Passant (Pawn capture). These are crucial for strategy.
days.tip: Castling can only happen if neither the King nor the Rook has moved and no squares are attacked.

days.title: Check, Checkmate, and Stalemate
days.description: Learn the conditions for Check, Checkmate (winning the game), and Stalemate (a draw). Play through 3 examples of each.
days.tip: A King in check must immediately move out of check, block the check, or capture the attacking piece.

days.title: Play your first full game (vs. AI)
days.description: Play a full game against a beginner-level AI on Chess.com or Lichess. Focus on moving all your pieces and not giving away pieces for free.
days.tip: Don't bring your Queen out too early; it can easily get attacked.

days.title: Opening principles: Control the center
days.description: Study the basic opening principles: control the center squares (d4, e4, d5, e5), develop your knights and bishops, and castle early.
days.tip: Moving the same piece multiple times in the opening wastes valuable time.

days.title: Week 1 review & goals
days.description: Reflect on your first game and what you've learned. Identify one area you want to focus on next week (e.g., protecting pieces, pawn structure).
days.tip: Reviewing your own games is one of the fastest ways to improve.
